title: Cost Scaling Across Building Sizes: Full-Time 40-Hour Custodian vs. Contract Cleaning
seoTitle: Scale Curve: Full-Time 40-Hour Custodian Cost at 5k, 15k & 35k Sq Ft
metaDescription: Scale curve for a full-time 40hr custodian across 5,000, 15,000, and 35,000 sq ft offices ($0.05-$0.15/sq ft). Run your square footage in our calculator.
excerpt: A full-time 40-hour in-house custodian represents a fixed 2,080-hour annual labor commitment, which creates wildly different cost-per-square-foot economics across 5,000, 15,000, and 35,000-square-foot commercial buildings. This scale curve analysis maps where a single W-2 custodian creates severe idle-time waste, where it hits peak productivity, and where it breaks down from overcapacity.
quickAnswer: Mapping the scale curve full time 40 hour custodian model reveals a rigid U-shaped efficiency curve: at 5,000 sq ft, a full-time W-2 custodian costs an unsustainable $1.10/sq ft per month ($66,000/yr) compared to $865–$1,250/month for an outsourced 3x–5x/week crew. At 15,000 sq ft, in-house cost drops to $0.37/sq ft monthly ($5,500/mo) versus $2,100–$3,200/mo outsourced, while at 35,000 sq ft a solo 40-hour custodian falls 17.5 hours per week short of the ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hr daily production benchmark, forcing either skipped deep-cleaning zones or $15,000+ in annual overtime.

blocks.text: The Fixed-Step Cost Problem: Why In-House W-2 Labor Does Not Scale Linearly

Outsourced commercial janitorial contracts scale along a smooth, continuous curve tied directly to cleanable square footage, restroom density, and service frequency. Under standard US pricing tiers, a 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft office pays $0.09 to $0.15 per square foot per visit, a 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft office drops to $0.07 to $0.12 per square foot, and a 25,000+ sq ft enterprise floorplate compresses to $0.05 to $0.10 per square foot (further discounted by a 0.90 frequency multiplier for 5x-weekly service across 21.65 monthly visits). You pay strictly for the exact fractional labor hours required to service the space.

By contrast, evaluating the scale curve full time 40 hour custodian option exposes a classic step-function trap. When a business commits to a full-time 40-hour-per-week W-2 employee, it locks in 2,080 paid clock hours per year (approximately 1,872 productive net hours after 208 hours of holidays, PTO, and sick leave) at a fixed burdened cost of $62,000 to $70,000 annually ($5,167 to $5,833 per month including FICA, Class 9014 workers' compensation, health benefits, equipment depreciation, and PTO backfill). Whether your building requires 8 hours of weekly cleaning or 55 hours of weekly cleaning, the W-2 payroll ledger remains locked at 40 regular hours until overtime kicks in at 1.5x base pay.

blocks.title: The Sweet-Spot Bandwidth of One 40-Hour Custodian: 21,000 to 25,000 Sq Ft
blocks.text: At the ISSA standard production rate of 3,500 sq ft per hour for daily office cleaning, one full-time custodian delivering 7.0 net cleaning hours per 8-hour shift (after 60 minutes of chemical prep, supply staging, and mandatory breaks) reaches 100% capacity at 24,500 sq ft per day. Any facility under 18,000 sq ft pays for unused custodial capacity; any facility over 26,000 sq ft suffers from chronic scope cutting.
5,000 vs. 15,000 vs. 35,000 Sq Ft: Side-by-Side Scale Curve Comparison

To illustrate how building square footage alters the financial and operational return of a full-time 40-hour custodian, examine the three benchmark tiers below. Each tier assumes a 5-day-per-week (21.65 visits per month) weekday cleaning requirement with mixed commercial carpet and VCT/tile wet zones (1.05 mixed flooring multiplier) and assumes a baseline burdened in-house custodian cost of $5,500 per month ($66,000/year before overtime or supplemental contract labor).

blocks.text: Tier 1 Analysis: The 5,000 Sq Ft Small Office (Severe Overcapacity)

In a 5,000-square-foot professional office with two restrooms, one breakroom, and 25 to 35 employees, core janitorial tasks take only 1.43 to 1.75 hours per evening. Hiring a full-time 40-hour W-2 custodian for a 5,000 sq ft footprint results in nearly 28 hours per week of idle payroll. Even if the facility cuts service to a 3x-weekly schedule (13.0 visits per month at a 0.95 frequency multiplier) or keeps 5x-weekly service with an outsourced vendor, a commercial cleaning company bills $1,050 to $1,480 per month. Paying $5,500 per month for a 40-hour employee in a 5,000 sq ft suite only occurs when the employee serves primarily as a warehouse shipping clerk, facilities runner, or building maintenance technician who cleans for 90 minutes at the end of the shift.
Tier 2 Analysis: The 15,000 Sq Ft Mid-Sized Facility (The Hybrid Porter Crossover)

At 15,000 square feet, daily cleaning requires roughly 4.3 hours per day (21.5 hours per week), plus 3.5 hours per week for restroom consumable stocking, interior glass partition detailing ($15–$35 per visit equivalent value), and breakroom appliance sanitation ($12–$25 per visit equivalent value). That leaves roughly 15 hours per week of remaining bandwidth inside a 40-hour schedule.

If the 15,000 sq ft tenant solely needs after-hours trash, vacuuming, and restroom sanitation, outsourcing to a night crew at $2,250 to $3,150 per month saves more than $28,000 per year. However, if the tenant operates a high-touch medical clinic, executive law firm, or customer briefing center where those remaining 15 hours per week are used for daytime coffee service resets, conference room turnarounds, and minor facilities repairs (replacing HVAC filters, painting scuffed drywall, and assembling standing desks), the 15,000 sq ft tier often represents the true operational crossover where an in-house 40-hour custodian earns their salary.
Tier 3 Analysis: The 35,000 Sq Ft Enterprise Building (The Production Bottleneck & Equipment Multiplier)

At 35,000 square feet, a single full-time 40-hour custodian hits a physical wall. Requiring 10.0 productive cleaning hours per day (50 net cleaning hours per week, or roughly 57 clock hours once setup and breaks are included), a 35,000 sq ft building overwhelms one worker. When management refuses to expand headcount or outsource, the lone custodian is forced to drop daily vacuuming to twice-weekly rotation, skip high-dusting and glass partitions, or rack up 15+ hours of weekly overtime at 1.5x pay ($2,145/month extra).

To stretch a single 40-hour custodian's reach from 24,500 sq ft toward 30,000+ sq ft without burning out the worker or triggering overtime, facilities must upgrade from upright vacuums (which clean roughly 2,500 sq ft/hr) to commercial HEPA backpack vacuums (which clean up to 5,000–7,400 sq ft/hr on open commercial carpet):

Atrix VACBP1 Ergo HEPA Commercial Backpack Vacuum: Engineered for 15,000 to 35,000 sq ft medical and corporate suites, the Atrix VACBP1 provides an oversized 8-quart debris capacity and 4-stage HEPA 99.97% filtration in a 10.3 lb ergonomic frame operating at 67 dBA, reducing bag-change stops during full-floor runs.

Powr-Flite BP6S Comfort Pro Backpack Vacuum: Built for daytime portering in occupied 15,000 to 35,000 sq ft offices, the 11 lb Powr-Flite BP6S features a 6-quart tank, 5-stage HEPA filtration, a cooling mesh lumbar harness, and a whisper-quiet 62 dBA sound profile that allows vacuuming during business hours without disrupting phone calls.

blocks.title: How Backpack Vacuums Shift the 35,000 Sq Ft Labor Curve
blocks.text: Replacing a 12-inch upright vacuum with a 14-inch floor-tool commercial backpack vacuum increases carpet production speed by up to 2.2x. In a 35,000 sq ft facility with 75% carpet coverage (26,250 sq ft), switching to a HEPA backpack vacuum shaves up to 2.8 hours off daily floor care—bringing a 35,000 sq ft building back inside a single 40-hour custodian's weekly capacity.

faqs.q: At what square footage does a full-time 40-hour custodian reach 100% capacity?
faqs.a: Under the ISSA standard office cleaning rate of 3,500 sq ft per hour, a single full-time 40-hour custodian delivering 35 productive cleaning hours per week reaches 100% capacity at 24,500 square feet on a 5x-weekly full-scope schedule. With high-speed HEPA backpack vacuums and spot-vacuuming rotation on low-traffic zones, one skilled custodian can stretch coverage to 30,000–32,000 square feet.

faqs.q: Why is an outsourced cleaning vendor cheaper at 15,000 sq ft than a single in-house employee?
faqs.a: A 15,000 sq ft office only requires about 4.3 labor hours per night (21.5 hours per week). An outsourced janitorial contractor deploys a 2-person crew for 2.15 hours per evening and only bills you for those 21.5 weekly hours (roughly $2,250–$3,150/month), whereas a full-time in-house custodian forces you to pay for 40 hours per week plus benefits and PTO backfill ($5,500/month).

faqs.q: How do flooring types affect the square-foot limit of a 40-hour custodian?
faqs.a: Polished concrete (0.95 labor multiplier) and commercial carpet tiles (1.00 multiplier) clean fastest with auto-scrubbers and HEPA backpack vacuums. Facilities with extensive ceramic tile and grout (1.12 multiplier) or hardwood floors (1.08 multiplier) reduce a single 40-hour custodian's daily square-foot ceiling by 8% to 12% due to wet-mopping dwell times and detail scrubbing.

faqs.q: What happens when a solo 40-hour custodian takes vacation in a 35,000 sq ft building?
faqs.a: Across 208 annual hours of combined federal holidays, paid vacation, and sick leave (over 5 full workweeks per year), a 35,000 sq ft facility with one in-house custodian has zero coverage unless management retains an on-call commercial janitorial vendor or temporary staffing agency at $38 to $55 per billable backfill hour.
